title: Retro Pixel vs Retro 90s
lede: Two kinds of nostalgia, ten years apart and often confused. One imitates a screen; the other imitates a browser.
verdict: Retro pixel is 8-bit: Press Start 2P, a headline that tops out at 1.9rem because bitmap type cannot scale, and a 3px neon border with a hard 4px offset. Retro 90s is HTML-era: Times New Roman on navy, bevels built from outset and ridge borders, and no radius anywhere.
brief: Pixel is constrained by the typeface. Press Start 2P is a grid of blocks, so the headline is clamp(1rem, 3.4vw, 1.9rem) — deliberately small, because at 4rem the glyphs stop looking like letters. Line height runs near double, borders are 3px solid #39ff14 with a 4px 4px 0 #1a5c1a shadow, and the hover state translates the element 2px into its shadow.

Retro 90s is not a font choice, it is a reconstruction of defaults: Times New Roman, navy #000080, yellow body text, and bevels made from border-style outset and ridge rather than from gradients. Buttons carry 3px outset #ffffff and flip to inset on hover. Radius is 0 on every element, because rounded corners did not exist yet.

dimensions.name: Hover
dimensions.b: border-style flips from outset to inset

whenA: The subject is games, and the pixel reference is understood by the audience immediately
You want short labels and big blocks rather than paragraphs
The page is a landing screen or a teaser, not a document
whenB: The joke or the affection is specifically the early web — fan pages, guestbooks, under-construction banners
You want a page that reads as software from a period, bevels included
The content is short; Times on navy at long length is genuinely hard to read
promptDelta: Both prompts need a size cap, for different reasons: pixel type is unreadable above about 2rem, and 90s type gets loud fast. Name the face and the cap together — "Press Start 2P, headline no larger than 1.9rem, line-height 2" or "Times New Roman, 3px outset borders, no border radius anywhere". Ask for "retro" alone and a model returns Y2K chrome roughly half the time, because that is the better documented reference.
